content: Norgestrel, a progestin hormone, is used as an oral contraceptive to prevent pregnancy. It works by thickening vaginal fluid to inhibit sperm from reaching an egg (fertilization). This medication is not suitable for emergency contraception and will not prevent pregnancy if used after unprotected sex. Additionally, it does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) such as HIV, hepatitis B, gonorrhea, or syphilis. To reduce the risk of infection, it is recommended to use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activity. When using this medication, take one tablet daily at the same time each day, even during bleeding or spotting. Do not skip doses, as this may reduce its effectiveness. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the medication after an evening meal or at bedtime may help. If you miss a dose or take it more than three hours late, use a backup contraceptive method, such as a condom, for additional protection. Norgestrel is not recommended during pregnancy. If you suspect you are pregnant, discontinue use and consult your doctor immediately. While small amounts of the medication may pass into breast milk, it is generally considered safe for nursing infants. According to the LactMed database, progestin-only contraceptives, such as norgestrel, are the preferred hormonal contraceptives during lactation. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, increased appetite, stomach cramping or bloating, dizziness, headaches, and irregular vaginal bleeding or spotting. These effects are more likely during the first few months of use. If these symptoms persist or worsen, contact your doctor promptly. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but require immediate medical attention. Certain medications and substances can interact with norgestrel, potentially reducing its effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Examples include drugs that induce or inhibit the CYP3A4 enzyme, such as rifampin, St. John’s Wort, or ketoconazole. Inform your doctor of all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking to avoid potential interactions. If you start a new medication, discuss whether you need to use a reliable backup contraceptive method. Norgestrel may interfere with some laboratory tests, potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel that you are using this medication. Store the tablets at room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F) away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Women who smoke and use oral contraceptives are at a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular events, such as heart attacks and strokes. Smoking cessation is strongly advised for all users of oral contraceptives. Additionally, norgestrel is contraindicated in individuals with known or suspected pregnancy, breast cancer, undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding, hypersensitivity to the medication, or active liver disease. Progestin-only contraceptives, such as norgestrel, prevent pregnancy by suppressing ovulation in approximately half of users, thickening cervical mucus to inhibit sperm penetration, reducing mid-cycle hormone peaks, slowing ovum movement through the fallopian tubes, and altering the endometrium. Irregular menstrual patterns, including spotting, missed periods, or prolonged amenorrhea, are common. If bleeding suggests infection, malignancy, or other abnormalities, these causes should be ruled out. If prolonged amenorrhea occurs, evaluate for pregnancy. Studies indicate a rapid return to normal ovulation and fertility after discontinuing progestin-only contraceptives. Long-term use of contraceptive doses of oral progestins has not been associated with adverse effects on fetal development. Small amounts of progestin may pass into breast milk, but no significant adverse effects on infant growth or development have been reported. If you experience symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, such as difficulty breathing, swelling, or severe dizziness, seek immediate medical attention. In the event of an overdose, contact a poison control center or emergency services immediately. For U.S. residents, call 1-800-222-1222; for Canadian residents, call 1-844-764-7669. This medication is generally safe and effective when used as directed. However, it is essential to consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and to address any concerns or questions about its use.
